summary.headline: Bosch Ltd Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13.3% YoY to INR55,657 million; FY26 PAT up 37.6% to INR27,702 million, aided by one-off divestment gains.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR55,657 million (+13.3% YoY), with EBITDA of INR7,815 million (+20.8%), led by Power Solutions and Two-Wheeler PowerSports. For FY26, revenue was INR200,347 million (+10.8%) and EBITDA INR26,503 million (+14.7%), with PAT of INR27,702 million (+37.6%) inflated by profit on sale of Building Technologies units (Video Solutions, Access and Intrusion, Communication Systems). Q4 PAT rose only 2.7% YoY. Management guided FY27 volumes as broadly flattish, citing West Asia and crude-price risks, and announced two JVs: one with Brakes India and Wheels India for commercial vehicle air systems, and the pending acquisition of Robert Bosch Chassis Systems.

financial_highlights.change: +37.6% YoY; boosted by profit on sale of Building Technologies units

segments.name: Power Solutions
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales grew 27.4% YoY and FY26 grew 17.6%; management said calendar 2025 net sales exceeded INR130 billion and Q4 sales were over INR14 billion. CAFE Phase 3 rollout is scheduled for 30 April 2027, starting January 2027 for new CV models.

segments.name: Two-Wheeler and PowerSports
segments.commentary: Q4 sales grew 63.4% YoY and FY26 grew 69.1%, driven by exhaust gas sensors from OBD2 norms effective 1 April 2025. Management said it met 100% delivery commitment to OEMs despite supply chain pressure.

segments.name: Mobility Aftermarket
segments.commentary: FY26 sales grew 3.7%; independent aftermarket stagnated under supply pressure, while OE (OEM filters and spark plugs) grew robustly. Exports grew about 17%, led by Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.

segments.name: Mobility (total)
segments.commentary: Q4 sales grew 23.3% YoY and FY26 grew 16.9%.

segments.name: Consumer Goods / Power Tools
segments.commentary: Q4 sales grew 14.3% YoY and FY26 grew 6.4%, helped by traditional trade range expansion and incentive schemes. Cordless segment grew double digits for another quarter; Cordless 3.0 campaign runs across 25 industrial clusters. Became first power tool company in India to get mandatory BIS certification for angle grinders, drills and hammers; launched GBM30 magnetic drill, its first locally sourced finished good.

guidance_outlook: FY27 outlook is 'cautious optimism'; management maintained a flattish volume outlook for Bosch, with capacity to ramp up if needed.

Industry outlook FY27: PC steady growth, CV stable, tractors stable (El Nino a downside risk), three-wheelers positive, two-wheelers healthy (below-normal monsoon a risk). West Asia conflict may weigh on Q1 demand.
Content per vehicle expected to keep rising in FY27, including CAFE 3 related content; details to come in later calls.
Commodity and currency risks and supply chain agility are key FY27 priorities; cost progress via localisation, design and productivity, and AI in plants.
Air-systems JV with Brakes India and Wheels India (TSF Group partner) expected to start operations end-2026, samples in 2027 and series readiness in 2028.
capex_capacity: Air-systems JV with Brakes India and Wheels India: registered office in Chennai, covering electronically controlled modules for air compression, air processing, air suspension and air parking brakes for LCV and MHCV (ICE and BEV); start of operations end-2026, subject to regulatory approvals.
Management said JV details and own capex are published, but did not provide funding requirement figures.
Robert Bosch Chassis Systems acquisition: minority shareholder approval obtained; regulatory approval pending. Financials not disclosed until closing.
Tata AutoComp JV: establishment mid-2026 on track; SOP expected Q3 calendar 2027 (first shipments; management confirmed this as Q3 FY28 in response to a query).
Plant productivity improving; AI rollout in plants to raise efficiency; NOx sensor production started at Abu Dhabi plant for export to Europe.
demand_pricing: Passenger vehicle demand accelerated into year-end on SUV traction, lean dealer inventory and GST benefits; tractor demand strong with rabi area coverage up about 1.59 million hectares YoY.
Independent aftermarket weak; OE demand robust.
Competitive market; cost pressure from commodities and energy, offset by localisation, negotiation and design changes.
Logistics costs from Strait of Hormuz disruption are not a tailwind for exports.
Management said the BS7 (Euro 7) transition is not a technology or manufacturing challenge, but timing depends on government legislation.

qa_highlights.question: Can Bosch outgrow industry volumes via content per vehicle, given flattish segment outlooks?
qa_highlights.answer: Content per vehicle rises continuously and is expected to continue in FY27; the volume outlook is kept flattish out of caution about West Asia and crude prices, with room to ramp up if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why use equal joint ventures (eAxle, air systems) rather than going alone, and does this change Tier 1 status?
qa_highlights.answer: Bosch has no presence in electronically controlled air-system modules; TSF Group brings pneumatics and hydraulics expertise and the partnership gets to market faster. Management said there is no change in Tier 1 role.

qa_highlights.question: Will the air-systems JV cover advanced or traditional brakes, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: It focuses on advanced electronically controlled, software-driven modules for CVs (trucks and buses, ICE and BEV), operations from end-2026; samples in 2027, series readiness in 2028. Orders are still to be won.

qa_highlights.question: Why were other expenses down 9% YoY and 10% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Last year had a large customer project; this year had better fixed-cost absorption and cost control, partly offset by forex losses.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guided flattish when customers reportedly expect high-single to double-digit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 was very strong and it is being conservative given Strait of Hormuz, Ukraine and wider geopolitical risks.

qa_highlights.question: Can Bosch India become a low-cost export hub for the Bosch Group?
qa_highlights.answer: Production is typically regional; exports rise only if commercially viable and landed cost is competitive. Logistics costs currently offset the benefit, though the Abu Dhabi NOx sensor line is raising export share to Europe.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and crude/energy price volatility could weigh on demand in Q1 FY27 and raise input costs.
El Nino and a below-normal monsoon could hit tractor and two-wheeler demand.
Chassis acquisition awaits regulatory approval; valuation and financial details withheld.
Air-systems and Tata AutoComp JVs depend on approvals and on winning orders; JV funding needs not quantified.
Post-divestment PAT base: FY26 PAT growth flattered by one-off gains; watch underlying Q4 PAT (only +2.7% YoY).
Euro 7 (BS7) timing depends on government legislation.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic on FY27: confident on content growth and the FY26 close, but deliberately conservative on volumes given geopolitical and energy risks. Management was evasive on Chassis acquisition financials and JV funding figures, citing pending regulatory approval.
key_quotes: We currently maintained a flattish outlook. But that doesn't mean -- like the year we closed, we have no issues ramping up when required or going much beyond as required.
We are confident that the government's continued focus on capital expenditure outlined in the budget will bolster domestic demand and create opportunities.
So, the joint venture aims to start first operations late '26.

adds.what: Air-systems JV with Brakes India and Wheels India (electronically controlled modules for LCV/MHCV air systems), Chennai
Tata AutoComp JV, SOP expected Q3 calendar 2027 (management confirmed as Q3 FY28)

growth.why: Management guided FY27 volumes as flattish (no numbers), "maintained a flattish outlook," with capacity to ramp if needed; growth-relevant additions are JVs (air-systems start end-2026, Tata AutoComp SOP Q3 CY27/FY28) with no disclosed capex or capacity size, so backing is vague.
